modeTips.t: A: Valve's official lineups give the Ivy smoke and the 'A Cross' smoke (both from the T spawn/T Main side), the 'Longdog' smoke onto Popdog, and the 'Z' smoke onto the Connector end of A. Typical execute: smoke Connector/Z, Heaven side and Ivy exit, molly E-box, then hit from T Main, Ivy and Popdog together. B: flash from Upper B, smoke the CT side (Back of B/Connector), molly Oil or Scaffolding, then enter from Upper B and B Ramp together.
modeTips.ct: Common setup: two or three A (Heaven/Hell, E-box or Popdog, one watching Ivy from Tunnel 1), one or two B (Scaffolding, Oil or Back of B), with the Connector as the rotation link. Early molly on the Ivy exit or Popdog slows fast A pushes.
modeTips.pistol: Ts often rush A through T Main and Popdog, or go Upper B. CTs: play close angles behind train cars; utility on Ivy and Popdog.
modeTips.retake: A: tunnels and Hell together, flash over the trains, check the Bombtrain top. B: Back of B and Connector together, flash Upper B, clear Oil and Scaffolding.
modeTips.postplant: A: hold from Ivy, T Main and the Bombtrain top. B: hold from Upper B and B Ramp; one player lurking near Popdog can catch rotators. C4 blast damage was reworked in July 2026 (Season 5): re-check safe distances in practice.

maps.setting: Skyscraper under construction high above a city: bare concrete floors, scaffolding, cranes, elevator shafts and open edges with a long fall. Bomb defusal map; removed from Active Duty in January 2025 (Train replaced it), still in Competitive, Casual, Retakes and Wingman.
maps.layout: Two floors. Ts spawn on the LOWER floor (50th) at the south and climb to the main UPPER floor (51st), where both sites, mid and CT spawn are. Use the USP-S or P2000 head-height precision against it

items.detail: Counter-Strike 2 (CS2), Valve, Source 2 engine. Released 27 September 2023 as the free-to-play replacement for CS:GO on Steam. Runs on Windows and Linux (no macOS client). 5v5 tactical shooter: Terrorists (T) plant the bomb on site A or B; Counter-Terrorists (CT) prevent or defuse it. Money earned each round buys weapons, armour and grenades.

items.name: Current build
items.detail: Game files list PatchVersion 1.41.9.2 dated Oct 22 2026 (steam.inf, SteamDatabase mirror). Small October 2026 updates were reported (one outlet: faster AUG reload and a ping icon for dropped defuse kits on Oct 8; unverified, not read from Valve notes).

items.name: Premier season
items.detail: Premier Season Five began in July 2026 (Valve notes date it 8 July; some sites say 6 July). Season medals need 25 Premier wins and an active CS Rating at season end (game UI text).

items.name: 2026 changes, first half
items.detail: March 18 2026: reload rework (a reload drops the current magazine and its bullets; reserve counted in magazines). July 8 2026: Premier Season Five, Cache in and Overpass out of Active Duty, bomb explosion redesign with damage baked per map. July 20/21 2026: the bomb blast clears smoke and puts out fire; the health-bar bomb damage preview shows only once the bomb is audible.

items.name: 2026 changes, second half
items.detail: Sept 22/23 2026 "Rush Hour": Rush 3v3 mode, Premier map picks instead of bans, silent reload (hold the key) and silent unscope, crosshair changes. Sept 25 fix added half outlines for crosshairs.

items.name: Game State Integration
items.detail: Valve's official Game State Integration (GSI) sends JSON to a local endpoint set in a cfg file: map, round phase, scores, bomb state, and for the local player health, armour, helmet, money, equipment value, weapons and ammo, round kills and headshot kills, and flashed, smoked and burning levels (0 to 255). Field names follow the Valve wiki page written for CS:GO (not re-checked for CS2).

items.name: Coaching policy note
items.detail: Sightline coaches live only offline or against bots; Premier, Competitive and other online matches get post-match coaching only. The coach reads the screen and Valve Game State Integration and never touches game memory or input.

items.name: Update 2026-01-21
items.detail: Anubis (reworked) returned to Active Duty; Train left the pool.; MP7: price $1,500 to $1,400, damage 29 to 30, range modifier 0.85 to 0.87 (less fall-off).; MP5-SD: price $1,500 to $1,400, damage 27 to 28, range modifier 0.85 to 0.87.; PP-Bizon: price $1,400 to $1,300 (no damage change).; Jump landing now uses sub-tick timing.

items.name: Update 2026-03-18
items.detail: ; Reserve ammo is now counted in magazines and retuned per weapon (for example AWP 2 spare magazines = 15 shots per round; AK-47 3; M4A4 4 = +30 rounds; Galil AR 4 = +50 rounds). ; Limited in-game map guides (annotations) in Competitive and Retakes for the first 5 rounds of each half (sv_allow_annotations_access_level 1, sv_annotation_limits_max_rounds_per_half 5).

items.name: Update 2026-03-18 (2)
items.detail: ; Friends can join Practice and Workshop map sessions from the friends list when Open Party is on.

items.name: Update 2026-07-06
items.detail: Cache replaced Overpass in Active Duty. Pool: Ancient, Anubis, Cache, Dust II, Inferno, Mirage, Nuke.; Soft CS Rating reset for the new season.; Start date reported as 6 July by most outlets, 8 July by one; the matching game build is dated 8 July 2026.

items.name: Update 2026-09-22
items.detail: ; Silent reload: hold the reload key to reload quietly but slowly. ; Crosshair overhaul: new Settings section Crosshair / Scopes, new styles, default style is now Dynamic Quad (cl_crosshairstyle 7); older crosshair codes were reported invalid. ; Clan tags returned; the Zeus x27 now hurts chickens; per-mode music volume settings.

items.name: Update 2026-10-08
items.detail: Dropped defuse kits now show a ping icon.; AUG reload shortened (game data: time before it can fire after starting a reload 3.77 s to 3.2 s).; Sound fixes (for example Desert Eagle silent-reload sound) and map clipping fixes on Rush.

items.name: Update 2026-10-14
items.detail: Competitive, Wingman and Casual configs now drop every grenade a player carried on death (mp_death_drop_grenade 2 to 3). Read from game files; official note wording not confirmed.

items.name: Update 2026-10-22
items.detail: New voice-chat audio processing options (WebRTC echo cancellation, gain control, noise suppression convars). Read from game files; no gameplay, HUD or economy change found.

items.name: Earlier change
items.detail: when: 2024 (spring). change: Incendiary price $600 to $500; CZ75-Auto kill reward $300 (was $100 in CS:GO); Zeus x27 kill reward $100.

items.name: Premier
items.detail: 5v5, MR12 (first to 13 of 24 rounds) with overtime, CS Rating (numbers, colour tiers). Since Sept 22/23 2026 a pick system replaced bans: Team 1 picks one map, Team 2 picks two, Team 1 picks a fourth, and one of the four is chosen at random. Active Duty pool only. A July 2026 update reportedly allowed 4-player premades (unverified).

items.name: Competitive
items.detail: 5v5 on a chosen map (or maps) with a Skill Group per map. MR12; a 12-12 score ends as a draw (no overtime by default, per guides). Settings in the Oct 2026 config: $800 start, $16,000 cap, 1:55 rounds, 15 s freeze time, 20 s buy time, friendly fire on (bullets do 33 percent to teammates), team collision on, Killer Replay off.

items.name: Wingman
items.detail: 2v2 on small maps, best of 16 rounds, $8,000 money cap, 1:30 rounds, 10 s freeze time, loss bonus $2,000 plus $300 per loss, Killer Replay off (Wingman config). Wingman map group in the game files: Debris, Eldorado, Poseidon, Overpass, Vertigo, Nuke, Inferno (display names unverified).

items.name: Casual
items.detail: 10v10, friendly fire off, team collision off, 50 percent kill rewards, best of 15 (game UI text). Good for relaxed practice; not representative of competitive economy.

items.name: Deathmatch
items.detail: Instant respawn, weapon chosen at spawn, 10-minute matches, points per kill. Used for aim warm-up.

items.name: Arms Race
items.detail: Gun-game: each kill upgrades your weapon; first to a Golden Knife kill wins. Instant respawn.

items.name: Retakes
items.detail: Official mode added October 2025: the bomb is already planted and CTs retake the site with set loadouts. Good practice for retakes and post-plants.

items.name: Rush
items.detail: Added Sept 2026: 3v3 through a gauntlet of battle arenas. Win a round by controlling the tower when time expires; win the match by capturing the enemy castle or winning 8 rounds (game UI text). Friendly fire on, armour purchasable.

items.name: Offline with bots / practice
items.detail: Local practice servers, workshop maps (aim_botz, Recoil Master, Yprac Hub prefire and utility maps) and offline matches with bots. This is where live coaching is allowed.

items.name: Active Duty pool (Premier Season Five, since July 2026)
items.detail: Ancient, Anubis, Cache, Dust II, Inferno, Mirage, Nuke. Cache returned for the first time in about seven years, replacing Overpass. The competitive map list in the Oct 2026 game files lists these seven first. Train left the pool earlier (one source says Anubis returned in its place on 22 January 2026; unverified).

items.name: Ancient
items.detail: Jungle temple map. Mid and the donut area connect to A; B is reached through a long ramp and cave. Guides call it CT-leaning; mid control is key.

items.name: Anubis
items.detail: Egyptian canal map with water in mid. Narrow chokes into both sites; the canal and connector make fast rotations for Ts.

items.name: Cache
items.detail: Industrial nuclear site map, reworked for 2026. Classic structure: A main, mid with Z-connector and highway, B main (squeaky door). Mid control splits the CTs. Exact 2026 rework callouts not verified here.

items.name: Dust II
items.detail: Desert classic: long A, short A (catwalk), mid doors and B tunnels. Long sightlines suit rifles and the AWP; mid control opens both sites.

items.name: Inferno
items.detail: Italian town: banana to B, apartments and short to A, mid. Close angles and heavy utility use; molotovs and smokes decide banana control.

items.name: Mirage
items.detail: Moroccan town: A ramp and palace to A, apartments to B, mid with window and connector. The most played map in Premier, per reports after the pick change.

items.name: Nuke
items.detail: Two sites stacked vertically (A upstairs, B below) with outside yard, ramp and vents. Fast CT rotations; guides call it CT-sided.

items.name: Reserve and other maps
items.detail: Overpass, Train and Vertigo are in reserve map groups in the game files; Office and Italy are hostage maps in Casual and Competitive.

items.name: Buy menu
items.detail: Opened in the buy zone during the freeze time and buy time (20 s in Competitive). Categories PISTOLS, SMGs, HEAVY, RIFLES, GEAR, GRENADES; weapon panels show COST, KILL AWARD, ARMOR PENETRATION, STOPPING POWER and more. Buttons: Re-Buy Previous, Auto Buy, Refund (sell back during buy time) and Hold to Buy and Throw (buy for a teammate).

items.name: Buy menu loadout
items.detail: A Dropped Weapons list shows nearby weapons. Which weapon fills each slot (M4A4 or M4A1-S, CZ75-Auto or Five-SeveN/Tec-9, Desert Eagle or R8, MP7 or MP5-SD) is set in the inventory loadout, so the menu differs between players.

items.name: Scoreboard (Tab)
items.detail: Per player: Money, K, A, D, MVPs (star), Score, HS%, ADR, KDR, UD (utility damage), EF (enemies flashed), DMG; a Loss Bonus column with a tooltip saying what your team will earn with a round loss. A Cycle Stats option shows extra columns. Teammates' money is visible; enemy money is not.

items.name: Round end
items.detail: Win panel with Terrorists Win or Counter-Terrorists Win and the reason: Bomb detonated, CTs eliminated, Bomb defused, Terrorists eliminated, or Bombing failed (time ran out), plus an MVP line (most eliminations, planting or defusing the bomb).

items.name: Round-end damage report
items.detail: Under the enemy portraits at the top of the screen the round-end report shows damage you gave (green fields) and took (dark fields) for each enemy. Guides say it is the only in-game damage readout in Competitive and Premier, and that it can be turned off (cl_disable_round_end_report, single source).

items.name: Death screen
items.detail: Competitive and Wingman have no Killer Replay (spec_replay_enable 0 in both configs). The view freezes briefly on the killer (spec_freeze_time 2 s) and the death panel appears: killer avatar with a health bar (their health left), killer name, "killed you with their <weapon>" and the weapon image. Then you spectate teammates only.

items.name: Death panel damage lines
items.detail: The Oct 2026 layout also has "Damage taken: X in N hits" and "Damage given: Y in N hits" rows with bars. Some players report damage no longer shows after death, so treat these rows as unverified until seen on screen.

items.name: Death panel special texts
items.detail: "You were killed by the C4 explosion", "You burned to death", "You were killed by your own grenade", "killed you with your own <weapon>" (killed with your dropped gun), "FINAL KILL of the round", and domination or revenge markers.

items.name: Killer Replay
items.detail: Exists in other modes (option Automatic Killer Replay; press Reload for Killer Replay). Off in Competitive and Wingman per the configs. When running, your player can be outlined.

items.name: Match end
items.detail: Final scoreboard and accolades such as The Executioner (most kills), The Pain Train (most damage), The Carry (highest ADR), The Bullseye (highest headshot percentage), The Tenderizer (most assists), The Trifecta and The Quad Killer (multi-kills). Premier shows the CS Rating change.

items.name: Halftime and overtime
items.detail: Sides swap after 12 rounds; money resets to $800 with the loss count at one. Overtime in Premier is played in 6-round blocks (3 per side); guides differ on start money ($10,000 default or $12,500).

items.name: Radar settings for the coach
items.detail: Make the radar a stable, north-up picture so the app can map icon pixels to map callouts and grid cells that match the official overview image. 00.

items.name: Kill feed
items.detail: Top right. Entry order: [eye icon if the killer was blind] killer [+ flashbang icon + assister, or + assister] [in-air icon] weapon [no-scope icon] [through-smoke icon] [wallbang icon] [headshot icon] victim. CT names blue, T names gold.

items.name: Kill feed: your entries
items.detail: Entries with you: your kills have a red outline, your deaths a dark red background. Entries last about 5 seconds, or 7.5 seconds when they involve you (game styles).

items.name: Radar
items.detail: Top left. Your arrow, teammates as coloured dots, enemies as red dots only when spotted by your team, the bomb (dropped, carried or planted) and bomb sites A and B.

items.name: Health and armour
items.detail: Bottom left: health (100 max) and armour value with a helmet icon when bought. Since July 2026 part of the health bar flashes red to preview bomb damage once the bomb is audible.

items.name: Weapon and ammo
items.detail: Bottom right: current weapon, bullets in the magazine and reserve. Since March 2026 reserve ammo is counted in magazines for most weapons.

items.name: Money
items.detail: Shown with the HUD during play and in the buy menu; teammates' money on the scoreboard. Max $16,000.

items.name: Team counter and timer
items.detail: Top centre: round timer between the two scores, player avatars per team (greyed when dead), or alive counts with the Large Player Count option. After the plant the timer is replaced by the bomb icon (no countdown is shown; players time it themselves).

items.name: Flash, smoke and fire
items.detail: A flash whites out the screen and fades; smoke appears as a grey cloud; fire shows flames and health loss. Game State Integration reports flashed, smoked and burning levels.

items.name: Damage indicator
items.detail: A red marker around the crosshair shows the direction of incoming damage.

items.name: Defuse and plant bars
items.detail: A progress bar appears while planting or defusing; a kit icon shows when a CT carries a defuse kit.

items.name: Options that change the look
items.detail: HUD scale, team overhead ID (When in View, or shown permanently with or without equipment), Large Player Count, crosshair style and outlines (half outlines since Sept 2026), round-end report on or off, Automatic Killer Replay. The vision model should not assume one fixed layout.

items.name: HUD: radar (top-left)
items.detail: Circular radar by default (about 250 px across inside a 300 px panel that starts about 40 px from the top, at 1080p). It turns square and shows the whole map while the Tab scoreboard is open (default) or at all times if Force Square Shape is on.

items.name: HUD: place name (directly under the radar, centred on it)
items.detail: Confirmed: CS2 shows the current place (callout) name of the local player under the radar as white text (radar layout element 'DashboardLabel', 22 px font). Names come from the map's navigation place names (for example 'Long Doors', 'BombsiteA').

items.name: HUD: team counter (top centre)
items.detail: Round timer (m:ss) in the middle with the CT score on its left and the T score on its right; player avatars for each team spread outwards (CT side left, T side right) with small health bars, dead players greyed with a skull; alive counts beside each team. Kill markers under an avatar show kills this round.

items.name: HUD: team counter (top centre) (2)
items.detail: During freeze time teammates' avatars can show money, best weapon, grenades, armour and kit. After a round, avatars show a damage report (damage given and taken).

items.name: HUD: bomb planted (top centre, in place of the timer)
items.detail: When the bomb is planted the timer is replaced by a red bomb icon with pulsing lines; there is no countdown number. A defused-bomb icon shows after a defuse. The planted bomb also appears on the radar.

items.name: HUD: money (bottom-left area, above the health and armour readout…
items.detail: Money as '$1,234' with a green shopping-cart icon while you are in the buy zone. Money gained flashes green, money spent flashes red. (Unverified.)

items.name: HUD: health armour (bottom-left)
items.detail: Health number with a cross icon and armour number with a shield icon (helmet outline when a helmet is worn), tinted by HUD Color (default: team colour).

items.name: HUD: ammo (bottom-right)
items.detail: Rounds in the magazine and reserve. Since Mar 2026 the reserve is shown as magazines, shells or bullets by weapon type, with a fill bar for the current magazine under the count.

items.name: HUD: inventory (right edge, lower half)
items.detail: Weapon list (primary, pistol, knife, grenades, C4) appears briefly when you switch weapons, or permanently with the inventory display setting in Settings > Game > Item (cl_showloadout 1).

items.name: HUD: kill feed (top-right, starting about 72 px from the top)
items.detail: Newest entry at the top; each lasts about 5 s (about 7.5 s if it involves you).

items.name: HUD: chat (lower-left, above the money)
items.detail: Team and all-chat messages and radio commands. (Unverified.)

items.name: HUD: centre messages (lower centre)
items.detail: Hint text, progress bars (planting and defusing), alerts.

items.name: HUD: win panel (upper centre, below the team counter)
items.detail: Round-end banner.

items.name: Radar 1
items.detail: Your own position: an arrow pointing where you look. With rotation on (default) the map turns and your arrow points up; with rotation off the map stays fixed and the arrow turns.

items.name: Radar 2
items.detail: Teammates: dots with a view cone. In Premier, Competitive and Wingman each teammate has a player colour (yellow, purple, green, blue or orange) that matches their avatar and scoreboard colour; with 'Colors and Letters' a letter is drawn too. In other modes teammates use the team colour (CT light blue, T yellow).

items.name: Radar 3
items.detail: Dead teammates: an X in their colour where they died.

items.name: Radar 4
items.detail: Enemies: a red dot (about #FF1919) while any player on your team can see them (spotted). When they leave sight a fading 'last seen' ghost marker remains briefly; you never see unspotted enemies.

items.name: Radar 5
items.detail: Dead enemies: a red X.

items.name: Radar 6
items.detail: Bomb: C4 icon on the carrier and where it is dropped (Terrorists see it; CTs see it once spotted, unverified). When planted, a bomb icon that flashes faster as detonation nears (three flash speeds in the layout).

items.name: Radar 7
items.detail: Bombsites: yellow 'A' and 'B' letters.

items.name: Radar 8
items.detail: Dropped defuse kit: kit icon (and a ping since 8 Oct 2026).

items.name: Radar 9
items.detail: Pings from teammates: expanding circles; speaking teammates: a green speaker icon on their dot.

items.name: Radar 10
items.detail: Teammates outside the visible radar area: arrows at the radar edge.

items.name: Radar 11
items.detail: Multi-level maps: small up or down markers on dots that are above or below your level.

items.name: Movement speeds
items.detail: Units per second, Oct 2026 data: knife 250; most pistols 240; MAC-10, MP9, PP-Bizon 240; P90 and UMP-45 230; M4A4 and M4A1-S 225; FAMAS and AUG 220; AK-47, Galil AR, XM1014 215; AWP 200 (100 scoped); Negev 150.

items.name: Accuracy and movement
items.detail: Inaccuracy rises steeply with speed: AK-47 0.0064 standing, 0.0048 crouching, 0.175 running; AWP 0.002 scoped standing, 0.176 moving. Community testing puts full accuracy below about 34 percent of a weapon's top speed. Counter-strafing (tapping the opposite key) stops you almost at once. Jumping shots are very inaccurate.

items.name: Recovery and recoil
items.detail: Spray adds inaccuracy that recovers over about 0.34 to 0.37 s for the main rifles when standing (AK-47 0.368 s, M4A4 0.339 s). Fire rate: AK-47 every 0.1 s (600 per minute), M4A4 every 0.09 s, M4A1-S every 0.1 s, AWP 1.455 s between shots. Recoil patterns are fixed per weapon and learnable.

items.name: Damage multipliers
items.detail: Head x4 (M4A1-S 3.475, Desert Eagle 3.9); chest x1, stomach x1.25, legs x0.75. Damage falls with range by the weapon range modifier per 500 units (AK-47 0.98, M4A1-S 0.94, MAC-10 0.80, UMP-45 0.75).

items.name: Armour
items.detail: Kevlar ($650) covers the body; the helmet (Kevlar and Helmet $1,000) covers the head. Armour penetration is half the armour ratio: AK-47 77.5 percent, M4s 70, AWP 97.5, Desert Eagle 93.2, Tec-9 90.6, Five-SeveN 91.2, USP-S 50.5, Glock-18 47.

items.name: One-tap facts (derived from game data)
items.detail: AK-47: one head hit kills through a helmet at normal ranges (about 112). M4A4 and M4A1-S: about 92 to a helmeted head, so two hits. Desert Eagle: one head hit through a helmet out to long range. USP-S (about 140) and Glock-18 (about 120) kill a helmetless head up close, the Glock only within about 500 units. AWP: any chest or stomach hit kills; a leg hit does not.

items.name: Tagging
items.detail: Being hit slows you down; the weapon you hold sets how much (shown as STOPPING POWER in the buy menu). Exact CS2 values were not found.

items.name: Penetration
items.detail: Rifles and the Desert Eagle have penetration power 2, AWP and SSG 08 2.5, pistols and SMGs 1 (Oct 2026 data), so rifles and snipers shoot through thin cover. Leetify says an average player gets at least one wallbang kill in about 40 percent of matches.

items.name: Reloads (March 2026 rework)
items.detail: A reload discards the bullets left in the magazine. Reserve per weapon: AK-47 3 magazines, M4A4 4, M4A1-S 3, AWP 2, Desert Eagle 3, USP-S 2, Glock-18 3. Attacks are blocked for about 2.5 s (AK-47) to 3.1 s (M4) after a reload starts. Since Sept 2026 holding the reload key gives a slower, silent reload.

items.name: Grenade prices and limits
items.detail: Flashbang $200, smoke $300, HE $300, molotov $400 (T), incendiary $500 (CT), decoy $50; limits 2 flashes and 4 grenades in total. All grenades drop on death in Competitive.

items.name: Grenade effects
items.detail: Smoke lasts roughly 18 to 20 s (guides differ). Fire deals about 40 HP per second: molotov about 7 s, incendiary about 5.5 s since May 2024. HE up to about 98 unarmoured, 57 armoured. Flash duration depends on angle and distance. Molotovs no longer break on players in flight (early 2026).

items.name: The bomb
items.detail: Bomb timer 40 s; defuse 10 s, or 5 s with a $400 kit. Explosion damage redesigned July 8 2026 (precomputed per map; no published values). Since July 20/21 2026 the explosion clears smoke and puts out fire nearby, and the health-bar damage preview appears once the bomb is audible. Plant time is about 3 s (unverified). A beta in October 2025 tested a defuse delay; no evidence it shipped.

items.name: Sound
items.detail: Running makes footsteps; walking and crouch-walking are silent, as are weapon switches. Jumps and landings make noise. Since Sept 2026 the held-key reload and unscoping are silent.

items.name: Sub-tick
items.detail: CS2 servers use sub-tick timing for inputs. Valve has made several fixes to movement and shot timing; guides say counter-strafing and peeker's advantage still work but feel different from CS:GO.

items.name: Start and cap
items.detail: $800 at the start of each half; $16,000 maximum (Oct 2026 config).

items.name: Round win
items.detail: $3,250 for elimination or time; $3,500 when the bomb explodes or is defused.

items.name: Loss bonus
items.detail: $1,400, then +$500 per consecutive loss, up to $3,400 ($1,400, $1,900, $2,400, $2,900, $3,400). Each half starts with one loss counted, so losing the pistol round pays $1,900. Most 2026 guides say a win lowers the count by one step rather than resetting it; some still describe a reset (unverified). The scoreboard tooltip shows your team's next loss income.

items.name: Objective money
items.detail: Planting player +$300; defusing player +$300. Ts who plant but lose the round get $600 extra each (cut from $800 in May 2024).

items.name: Kill rewards
items.detail: Default $300 (rifles, pistols, P90). SMGs $600 (MAC-10, MP9, MP7, MP5-SD, UMP-45, PP-Bizon). Nova, MAG-7, Sawed-Off $900; XM1014 $600. AWP $100. Zeus x27 $100. Knife $1,500. Casual pays 50 percent. Killing a teammate costs $300.

items.name: Pistol and SMG prices (Oct 2026)
items.detail: Pistols: Glock-18, USP-S, P2000 $200; P250 $300; Dual Berettas $300; Tec-9, Five-SeveN, CZ75-Auto $500; R8 $600; Desert Eagle $700. SMGs: MAC-10 $1,050; UMP-45 $1,200; MP9 $1,250; PP-Bizon $1,300; MP7, MP5-SD $1,400; P90 $2,350.

items.name: Gear prices
items.detail: Kevlar $650; Kevlar and Helmet $1,000; defuse kit $400 (CT); Zeus x27 $200.

items.name: Typical full buys
items.detail: T: AK-47, Kevlar and Helmet, smoke, two flashes, molotov = $4,800. CT: M4, Kevlar and Helmet, kit, smoke, two flashes, incendiary = $5,500. An AWP full buy costs about $1,850 to $2,050 more than the rifle version.

items.name: Buy types
items.detail: Full buy: rifle, armour and full utility. Eco (save): spend little or nothing to full buy next round. Force buy: spend everything on the best you can. Half buy: some gear while keeping enough for a full buy next round. Guides suggest a full eco below about $2,000 each after a loss and forcing around $2,500 to $3,500 before a bonus round; numbers differ between sources.

items.name: Pistol round and second round
items.detail: Pistol round: $800 each, usually Kevlar alone or a pistol upgrade plus a grenade. The pistol winners often anti-eco with SMGs for the $600 kill reward; the losers ($1,900 plus kill money) usually save or force.

items.name: Economy: round win rewards
items.detail: elimination: 3250. bombDefused: 3500. bombExploded: 3500. timeExpired: 3250. notes: Team income per player on the winning team. CTs win on time if no bomb is planted when the clock runs out.

items.name: Economy: loss bonus
items.detail: base: 1400. step: 500. max: 3400. ladder: 1400; 1900; 2400; 2900; 3400. startingLosses: 1. pistolRoundLoss: 1900. formula: Loss income = $1,400 + $500 x min(L, 4), where L is the team's loss counter before this loss. L starts at 1 (mp_starting_losses 1), goes up by 1 on each loss and goes down by 1 on each win..

items.name: Economy: loss bonus (2)
items.detail: cs2Rule: CS2 (mp_consecutive_loss_aversion 1): a round win steps the loss counter down by one instead of resetting it, so a team that wins one round after a losing streak still gets a high loss bonus if it loses again. CS:GO reset it to zero.. onWin: Counter minus 1 (not reset)..

items.name: Economy: loss bonus (3)
items.detail: resetAtHalf: Money resets to $800 at half-time; the counter is understood to return to its starting value (unverified).. readOnScreen: The Tab scoreboard shows a 'Loss Bonus' value with the tooltip '{team} will earn $X with a round loss'. Read it there instead of computing it.. consecutive_round_losses (available while playing)..

items.name: Economy: loss bonus (4)
items.detail: noIncomeOnTimeLoss: Terrorists still alive when they lose on time get no loss income (UI string: '+$0 penalty for running out of time').. unverified: true

items.name: Economy: plant bonus
items.detail: amount: 600. rule: If the bomb was planted but the Terrorists still lose the round, each Terrorist gets extra team income ('team income for planting the bomb'), on top of the loss bonus.. note: The shipped CS2 competitive cfg sets cash_team_planted_bomb_but_defused 600. Many older guides (CS:GO) say $800. Confirm with the in-game money notice.. unverified: true

items.name: Economy: per dead enemy team income
items.detail: amount: 50. rule: Since July 2025 a team income of $50 per enemy eliminated is shown at round end ('+$X team income for N eliminated terrorists/CTs'; convar cash_team_per_dead_enemy 50).. note: Coverage described it as a CT economy change; both team strings exist in the game files, so whether Terrorists also get it is unverified.. unverified: true

items.name: Economy: short handed bonus

items.name: Game State Integration
items.detail: Game State Integration (GSI) is Valve's built-in feature: the game reads cfg files named gamestate_integration_*.cfg at launch and HTTP-POSTs JSON game state to the uri in each file. Nothing reads game memory. While you play, it reports only your own state plus map and round info; all-player, position, grenade, bomb and countdown data arrive only when spectating, on GOTV or in demos.

items.name: Roles
items.detail: Entry (first in, takes the first fight), support (utility for the entry, trades), lurker (plays away from the team to catch rotations), AWPer, anchor (CT who holds a site), rotator, in-game leader (IGL: calls buys and strategy). Roles overlap: an IGL can lurk, an AWPer can entry.

items.name: T side round shape
items.detail: Default (spread out, take map control, gather information) then a mid-round call: execute (grouped utility and entry on one site), split (one site from two directions), fake (pressure one site, hit the other) or a fast hit. Plant, then post-plant crossfires and utility to stop the defuse.

items.name: CT side round shape
items.detail: Usual setup of two players on each site and one in mid or a rotating role (map-dependent). Play for information early, delay with utility, rotate on a count or a plant, crossfire on site, keep utility for the retake.

items.name: Opening duels
items.detail: SCOPE.GG 2026 data (Premier and FACEIT): the team with the opening kill wins about 65 to 73 percent of rounds depending on map and side.

items.name: Economy strategy
items.detail: Buy together; plan two rounds ahead with the loss bonus; save lost rounds; drop for teammates; anti-eco with discipline.

items.name: Clutch numbers
items.detail: One analysis of more than 200,000 pro matches (2021) put 1v2 wins near 19 percent, 1v3 near 4 percent and 1v4 near 0.6 percent (unverified). Leetify 2025 recaps of ordinary players show 1v1 win rates mostly 55 to 68 percent and 1v2 around 23 to 26 percent.

items.name: Map sides
items.detail: Guides describe Nuke and Ancient as CT-leaning (Overpass was the most CT-sided before leaving the pool). Side balance shifts with patches.

items.name: Numbers: ADR (average damage per round)
items.detail: Average 60 to 75 in matchmaking (guides); good 75 to 90; pros About 70 to 80 for most pros; star players 85 to 100 (one source lists ZywOo at 97.1 for 2025, unverified). Role matters: AWPers and entries trend higher, supports and anchors lower. Judge over many matches. Shown on the scoreboard and the end screen.

items.name: Numbers: KAST
items.detail: Average No published matchmaking average found; good 70 percent or more; pros About 68 to 75 percent for most pros; top players 75 to 80 percent. Kill, assist, survived or traded. Trade window usually 5 s (awpy default); HLTV does not publish its window. A high KAST means the player rarely has a round with no impact.

items.name: Numbers: HLTV Rating 3.0
items.detail: Average 1.00 by design; good Above 1.05 over a long sample; pros Top-20 players usually about 1.10 to 1.40 (approximate, not from a published table); event highs above 1.5. Rating 3.0 replaced 2.1 on 20 August 2025: adjusted for economy and round swing; an Oct 2025 tweak raised kill weighting to 25 percent and cut round swing to 33 percent. Formula not published. Pro-only stat.

items.name: Numbers: Leetify Rating
items.detail: Average 0 (zero-sum); good Positive over a long sample; pros Not published for pros. Built from changes in round win probability; credit split 35 percent kill, 30 percent damage, 20 percent trade, 15 percent flash assist.

items.name: Numbers: Leetify Aim Rating (0 to 100)
items.detail: Average 50 for the whole player base; good Above your rank bracket average; pros The 25,000+ Premier bracket average shown on profiles is about 89. Scores compare your aim stats with the average player using z-scores; Leetify recalibrated to newer data, which lowered scores for the same raw numbers.

items.name: Numbers: Headshot kill percentage
items.detail: Average About 46 percent for the Leetify average-player comparison (profile pages); good 45 percent and up for riflers; pros Very role-dependent: AWPers can sit near 20 to 35 percent, riflers often 45 to 55 percent. FACEIT samples at mid to high levels show about 38 to 45 percent. A high HS% with low kills can mean slow, cautious aim; read it with ADR.

items.name: Numbers: Opening duel win rate
items.detail: Average 50 percent by definition; good 55 percent or more for an entry; pros Pro samples range about 39 to 63 percent. The team with the opening kill wins about 65 to 73 percent of rounds (SCOPE.GG, Premier and FACEIT, 2026). Entries take more opening duels and lose more of them; judge with trades.

items.name: Numbers: Trade kills as a share of kills
items.detail: Average No published average found; good About 20 percent for supports and second players in; pros Pro snapshots about 15 to 25 percent (one stats site, undated; unverified). Also check traded deaths: deaths that a teammate trades within 5 s still count towards KAST.

items.name: Numbers: Leetify time to damage
items.detail: Average About 700 ms at low ranks; about 550 to 610 ms in mid and higher brackets (rank averages on profiles); good Under about 500 ms; pros Not published; strong individual values in 2025 recaps reach about 270 to 450 ms. Time from first seeing an enemy to first damaging them; combines crosshair placement, accuracy, fire rate and reaction. Values of 1 s or more are excluded.

items.name: Numbers: Leetify crosshair placement
items.detail: Average About 12 degrees at low ranks; about 8 degrees at Premier level (rank averages on profiles); good Under about 7 degrees; pros Not published; strong individual values in 2025 recaps reach about 4 degrees. Average angle the crosshair moved from first seeing an enemy to damaging them.

items.name: Numbers: Leetify proper counter-strafing
items.detail: Average About 75 to 83 percent (rank averages on profiles); good 85 percent or more; pros Not published; 90 percent and above seen on strong profiles. Share of shots fired after a good stop. Figures from individual Leetify profiles, not a published table.

items.name: Numbers: Enemies flashed and flash assists
items.detail: 7 enemies per flashbang ranked in the top 10 percent of Leetify users (2025 recaps); pros Not published. Figures come from individual Leetify 2025 recap pages, which rank a player against all users; flash assists of about 5 to 6 per match ranked in the top 20 percent or better. Scoreboard EF shows enemies flashed in the match.

items.name: Numbers: Utility damage
items.detail: Average No published average found; good About 150 HE damage per match ranked in the top 2 percent of Leetify users (2025 recap); pros Not published. Scoreboard UD column shows utility damage in the match. Use your own trend rather than a fixed target.

items.name: Numbers: Clutch win rate
items.detail: Average Leetify 2025 recaps: 1v1 mostly 55 to 68 percent, 1v2 about 23 to 26 percent (ordinary players); good Above those figures over a long sample; pros One 2021 analysis of 200,000+ pro matches: 1v2 about 19 percent, 1v3 about 4 percent, 1v4 about 0.6 percent (unverified). Small samples swing a lot; clutch rates depend on how often you are left in winnable spots.

items.name: Numbers: Kill/death ratio
items.detail: Average 1.00 across all players by definition; good Above 1.10 over many matches; pros Top players about 1.2 to 1.5 (approximate, not from a published table). Entries and supports often sit below 1.00 while helping the team; read with KAST and trades.

items.name: Numbers: Premier CS Rating
items.detail: Average Median about 10,900 to 11,000 (MetaBot sample Oct 2026; other sites quote about 8,900); good Top 25 percent from about 13,800; top 10 percent from about 17,400; pros Top 5 percent about 20,000; top 1 percent about 23,400 (other sites say about 27,000). Valve publishes no distribution; all figures are third-party samples and disagree.

items.name: Numbers: Average time to death in a round
items.detail: Average No published benchmark found; good Not available; pros Not available. Not tracked by the main public stat sites in a form found during this research; treat as an internal metric and compare a player with themselves.

items.name: Beginner (Silver to Gold Nova, Premier under about 10,000, FACEIT 1 to 3)
items.detail: Shooting while moving, crosshair on the floor, spraying at range, jumping shots, no armour on gun rounds, buying differently from the team, dying with grenades, self-flashing, standing in fire, reloading in the open, crossing open lanes, no defuse kit, dying to the bomb, fighting lost rounds instead of saving, running next to enemies.

items.name: Intermediate (Premier about 10,000 to 20,000, FACEIT 4 to 7)
items.detail: Untraded entries, re-peeking the same angle, dry peeking the AWP, CTs wide swinging, rotating on one sound, lone retakes, hunting after the plant, sticking the defuse with enemies alive, dumping utility early, lone peeks on anti-ecos, forcing every round, AWP not repositioning, throwing away numbers advantages, five players through one door.

items.name: Advanced (Premier 20,000+, FACEIT 8 to 10)
items.detail: Same spot and timing every round, staggered executes, split groups arriving apart, late hits, fakes with all five, lurks with no timing, early CT deaths without information, crossfires too close together, taking two enemies at once in clutches, not dropping for teammates.

items.name: Rank boundaries
items.detail: The rank bands are coaching conventions, not Valve tiers. Premier ratings: median about 10,900 to 11,000 (MetaBot sample, Oct 2026; other sites quote about 8,900), top 10 percent about 17,400, top 5 percent about 20,000, top 1 percent about 23,400 (sources disagree).

items.name: Shooting while running (beginner)
items.detail: Your view keeps sliding as you fire; tracers land wide of the crosshair; the death panel shows several shots and little damage. The fix is in the playbook: Counter-strafe before you shoot.

items.name: Crosshair aimed at the floor (beginner)
items.detail: While moving, the crosshair sits low or on walls; when an enemy appears it travels a long way up before the first shot. The fix is in the playbook: Crosshair at head level, on the next angle.

items.name: Spraying at long range (beginner)
items.detail: Holding the trigger on a distant target; tracers climb above the head; the magazine empties without a kill. The fix is in the playbook: Spray, burst or tap by range.

items.name: Jumping into fights with a rifle (beginner)
items.detail: The view rises and falls as you fire; the kill feed shows your death with the enemy standing still. The fix is in the playbook: Counter-strafe before you shoot.

items.name: Playing a gun round with no armour (beginner)
items.detail: HUD shows 0 armour while you carry a rifle or SMG; you die to two or three body shots. The fix is in the playbook: Buy together.

items.name: Buying differently from the team (beginner)
items.detail: Scoreboard in the freeze time: you buy a rifle while teammates keep pistols, or the reverse. The fix is in the playbook: Buy together.

items.name: Dying with grenades unused (beginner)
items.detail: HUD inventory still shows grenades at the moment of death; scoreboard UD and EF stay near 0. The fix is in the playbook: Support: utility first, then trade.

items.name: Flashing yourself or your team (beginner)
items.detail: Your screen turns white just after your own or a teammate's flash, before a fight. The fix is in the playbook: Pop flashes and team flashes.

items.name: Standing in fire (beginner)
items.detail: Flames on screen and health falling; death panel "You burned to death" or a molotov icon in the kill feed. The fix is in the playbook: Play around enemy utility.

items.name: Reloading in the open (beginner)
items.detail: Reload animation playing or the ammo counter at 0 when you die, often just after a kill. The fix is in the playbook: Reload behind cover, not in the fight.

items.name: Walking across open lanes (beginner)
items.detail: Radar shows you in an open area; no smoke or flash in the lane; killed at long range. The fix is in the playbook: Do not die in the open.

items.name: No defuse kit on a CT full buy (beginner)
items.detail: HUD has no kit icon on a full buy; you start a 10-second defuse late in the round. The fix is in the playbook: Defuse safely.

items.name: Dying to the bomb (beginner)
items.detail: Death panel: "You were killed by the C4 explosion"; your health bar flashed red before the explosion. The fix is in the playbook: Do not die to the bomb.

items.name: Fighting a lost round instead of saving (beginner)
items.detail: Team counter shows you alone against three or more; you take a fight and lose your rifle or AWP. The fix is in the playbook: Last alive: save or play.

items.name: Losing the rifle after the save call (beginner)
items.detail: The round is lost on the team counter, yet you stay near the enemy path or the bomb and die with a rifle or the AWP in the last seconds. The fix is in the playbook: Save when the round is lost.

items.name: Running next to enemies (beginner)
items.detail: You move at full speed (no walk) up to an angle you want to surprise; the enemy is already aimed at your path. The fix is in the playbook: Sound discipline.

items.name: Entering with nobody to trade (intermediate)
items.detail: Kill feed: you die first and no teammate kills your killer within 5 seconds; radar shows teammates far behind. The fix is in the playbook: Entry with support.

items.name: Re-peeking the same angle (intermediate)
items.detail: You get a kill or take damage, then show at the same corner within a few seconds and die. The fix is in the playbook: Do not re-peek the same angle.

items.name: Dry peeking an AWP (intermediate)
items.detail: Kill feed: AWP icon on your death; you appear in a long lane with no smoke or flash. The fix is in the playbook: Shoulder peek the AWP, then punish.

items.name: Wide swinging as a CT (intermediate)
items.detail: As CT you move towards the attackers after a flash or into a smoke, and die with 0 damage given. The fix is in the playbook: Hold angles and off-angles as a defender.

items.name: Rotating on a single sound (intermediate)
items.detail: Radar: you leave your site early in the round with no count called; the bomb is planted where you were. The fix is in the playbook: Rotate on information, not on noise.

items.name: Retaking alone (intermediate)
items.detail: Kill feed: CT deaths one at a time on the retake; radar shows no teammate near you as you enter. The fix is in the playbook: Retake together.

items.name: Hunting CTs after the plant (intermediate)
items.detail: Bomb planted with plenty of time; you leave your post-plant angle and die away from the bomb. The fix is in the playbook: Post-plant: crossfire and play the time.

items.name: Sticking the defuse with enemies alive (intermediate)
items.detail: Defuse bar on screen at death; no smoke on the bomb; the team counter shows Ts still alive. The fix is in the playbook: Defuse safely.

items.name: Throwing all utility at the first noise (intermediate)
items.detail: HUD grenade slots empty before the plant; nothing left for the retake. The fix is in the playbook: Save utility for the retake.

items.name: Lone peeks against an eco (intermediate)
items.detail: Enemy money low on the scoreboard; you die to a pistol in a close corner while holding a rifle. The fix is in the playbook: Anti-eco discipline.

items.name: Forcing every round (intermediate)
items.detail: Scoreboard money stays under $2,000 for several rounds; buys are mixed; the Loss Bonus tooltip is ignored. The fix is in the playbook: Know the loss bonus.

items.name: AWP staying on the same angle after a shot (intermediate)
items.detail: Kill feed: your AWP kill followed within seconds by your death at the same spot. The fix is in the playbook: AWP: reposition and do not overpeek.

items.name: Throwing away a numbers advantage (intermediate)
items.detail: Team counter shows your side ahead; you take a solo fight and die untraded; the round is lost. The fix is in the playbook: Mid-round: play the numbers.

items.name: Five players through one door (intermediate)
items.detail: Radar: all teammates in a line in one choke; one spray or one molotov hits several of them. The fix is in the playbook: Trade your teammates.

items.name: Same spot and timing every round (advanced)
items.detail: Radar at death shows the same position several rounds running; the killer is already aimed at it. The fix is in the playbook: Use or deny peeker's advantage.

items.name: Staggered execute utility (advanced)
items.detail: Smokes and flashes land over 10 or more seconds; teammates arrive on site one by one. The fix is in the playbook: Execute together.

items.name: Split groups arriving apart (advanced)
items.detail: Kill feed: deaths from one group, then the other group 10 seconds later. The fix is in the playbook: Split hits.

items.name: Hitting the site too late (advanced)
items.detail: Round timer under 0:20 before the hit starts; round ends with "Bombing failed". The fix is in the playbook: Use the clock on attack.

items.name: Faking with the whole team (advanced)
items.detail: Radar: all five Ts on the fake site; the real hit starts with very little time left. The fix is in the playbook: Fakes that sell.

items.name: Lurk with no timing (advanced)
items.detail: Radar: the lurker dies alone early, or arrives after the team has already lost the site. The fix is in the playbook: Lurk with purpose.

items.name: Dying early as CT with no information (advanced)
items.detail: Kill feed: first death of the round as CT with more than 1:30 on the clock and 0 damage given. The fix is in the playbook: Play for information first.

items.name: Crossfire partners too close together (advanced)
items.detail: Radar: two CTs in the same spot; one attacker kills both within a second or two. The fix is in the playbook: CT setups and crossfires.

items.name: Taking two enemies at once in a clutch (advanced)
items.detail: Last alive; you peek a spot where two enemies can see you and die to the second one. The fix is in the playbook: Clutch: one fight at a time.

items.name: Not dropping for teammates (advanced)
items.detail: Scoreboard: you start a round with $9,000 or more while a teammate plays with a pistol. The fix is in the playbook: Drop weapons for teammates.

items.name: Eco
items.detail: A save round: buy little or nothing to afford a full buy next round.

items.name: Full eco
items.detail: Spend nothing (or almost nothing) on a save round.

items.name: Force buy
items.detail: Spend all your money on the best gear you can, even if it leaves you unable to buy next round.

items.name: Half-buy
items.detail: Buy some gear while keeping enough money for a full buy next round.

items.name: Full buy
items.detail: Rifle (or AWP), armour, utility, and a kit for CTs.

items.name: Anti-eco
items.detail: Your buy against an opponent on an eco; usually SMGs or cheap rifles and careful play.

items.name: Bonus round
items.detail: The round after winning a pistol round, played with the weapons and money from that win.

items.name: Loss bonus
items.detail: Extra money paid to the losing team, rising with consecutive losses ($1,400 to $3,400).

items.name: Save
items.detail: Avoiding fights in a lost round to keep your weapon for the next round.

items.name: Exit frag
items.detail: A kill taken at the end of a lost round while saving.

items.name: Drop
items.detail: Buying a weapon and giving it to a teammate (buy menu: Hold to Buy and Throw).

items.name: Entry
items.detail: The first player into a site or area; the entry fragger takes the first fight.

items.name: Opening duel
items.detail: The first fight of the round; the opening kill gives a numbers advantage.

items.name: Trade
items.detail: Killing the enemy who just killed your teammate, usually within about 5 seconds.

items.name: Refrag
items.detail: Another word for a trade kill.

items.name: Lurk
items.detail: Playing away from the team, often alone and quiet, to catch rotations or flanks.

items.name: Rotate
items.detail: A CT moving from one site to the other; also Ts moving to a new target.

items.name: Over-rotation
items.detail: Too many CTs rotating, too early, leaving a site open.

items.name: Stack
items.detail: Three or more CTs on one site.

items.name: Gamble stack
items.detail: A stack placed on a guess about where the Ts will go.

items.name: Anchor
items.detail: A CT who holds a bombsite, often alone, and stays for the retake.

items.name: Crossfire
items.detail: Two players covering the same area from different angles.

items.name: Off-angle
items.detail: A non-standard holding spot that attackers do not usually pre-aim.

items.name: Pre-aim
items.detail: Placing your crosshair where an enemy will appear before you see them.

items.name: Prefire
items.detail: Shooting a spot where an enemy is very likely to be, as you peek it.

items.name: Crosshair placement
items.detail: Keeping the crosshair at head height on likely enemy positions.

items.name: Peek
items.detail: Moving out from cover to see or shoot an angle.

items.name: Dry peek
items.detail: A peek with no utility or support.

items.name: Jiggle peek
items.detail: A quick strafe out and back to gather information or bait a shot.

items.name: Shoulder peek
items.detail: Showing only your shoulder to bait a shot, usually from an AWP.

items.name: Wide swing
items.detail: A fast, wide peek that commits to a fight.

items.name: Peeker's advantage
items.detail: The moving player seeing the holder slightly earlier than the reverse.

items.name: Counter-strafe
items.detail: Tapping the opposite movement key to stop instantly before shooting.

items.name: Tap
items.detail: A single shot, letting the weapon reset between shots.

items.name: Burst
items.detail: Two to five shots, then a pause to reset.

items.name: Spray
items.detail: Holding the trigger while pulling against the recoil pattern.

items.name: Spray transfer
items.detail: Moving your spray from one enemy to another without stopping.

items.name: One-tap
items.detail: A kill with a single bullet, usually a head hit.

items.name: Wallbang
items.detail: A kill through a wall or other cover; marked by an icon in the kill feed.

items.name: Molly
items.detail: Molotov or incendiary grenade.

items.name: Nade
items.detail: A grenade; often means an HE grenade.

items.name: HE
items.detail: High-explosive grenade; up to about 98 damage unarmoured.

items.name: Flash
items.detail: Flashbang; blinds players who can see it when it pops.

items.name: Pop flash
items.detail: A flash that goes off quickly over a corner so the enemy cannot turn away.

items.name: Flash assist
items.detail: Flashing an enemy who is then killed by a teammate; shown with a flashbang icon in the kill feed.

items.name: Smoke
items.detail: Smoke grenade; blocks vision for roughly 18 to 20 seconds.

items.name: One-way smoke
items.detail: A smoke placed so one side can see feet or bodies under or past it and the other cannot.

items.name: Utility (util)
items.detail: All grenades: smokes, flashes, molotovs, HEs, decoys.

items.name: UD
items.detail: Utility damage, a scoreboard column.

items.name: EF
items.detail: Enemies flashed, a scoreboard column.

items.name: Lineup
items.detail: A fixed aim point and throw used to land a grenade in the same place every time.

items.name: Jumpthrow
items.detail: Jumping and throwing at the same moment for consistent grenade distance (often bound to one key).

items.name: Run-throw
items.detail: A throw while running, which adds distance.

items.name: Exec (execute)
items.detail: A planned site take with grouped utility.

items.name: Split
items.detail: An attack on one site from two directions at once.

items.name: Fake
items.detail: Showing pressure on one site to pull defenders before hitting the other.

items.name: Default
items.detail: A spread-out T setup that takes map control and gathers information before a call.

items.name: Map control
items.detail: Owning areas of the map so your team can move freely.

items.name: Rush
items.detail: A fast hit straight onto a site; also the 3v3 mode added in 2026.

items.name: Retake
items.detail: CTs taking a site back after the bomb is planted.

items.name: Post-plant
items.detail: The T phase after planting: holding angles on the bomb.

items.name: Default plant
items.detail: The usual spot to plant on a site.

items.name: Clutch
items.detail: Winning a round as the last player alive against one or more enemies.

items.name: 1vX
items.detail: A clutch situation: one player against X enemies.

items.name: Ace
items.detail: One player killing all five enemies in a round.

items.name: Ninja defuse
items.detail: Defusing unseen while Ts are still alive.

items.name: Fake defuse
items.detail: Tapping the defuse key briefly to bait a T into peeking.

items.name: Stick (the defuse)
items.detail: Committing to the full defuse without stopping.

items.name: Tap the bomb
items.detail: A short defuse start to bait or test for enemies.

items.name: Kit
items.detail: Defuse kit ($400); halves the defuse time to 5 seconds.

items.name: Boost
items.detail: Standing on a teammate to reach a higher spot.

items.name: Hold
items.detail: Watching an angle and waiting for the enemy to appear.

items.name: Info
items.detail: Information about enemy numbers, positions and weapons.

items.name: Call
items.detail: A short spoken message to the team; also the IGL decision.

items.name: IGL
items.detail: In-game leader: calls buys and strategy.

items.name: AWPer
items.detail: The player who uses the AWP sniper rifle.

items.name: Rifler
items.detail: A player who uses assault rifles as their main role.

items.name: KAST
items.detail: Share of rounds with a kill, assist, survival or traded death.

items.name: ADR
items.detail: Average damage per round (damage to each enemy is capped at their health).

items.name: HLTV Rating
items.detail: HLTV's performance rating; 1.00 is average. Rating 3.0 since August 2025.

items.name: Leetify Rating
items.detail: Leetify's rating based on changes in round win chance; 0 is average.

items.name: CS Rating
items.detail: Premier rating number with colour tiers.

items.name: Skill Group
items.detail: Competitive rank per map (Silver to Global Elite).

items.name: MR12
items.detail: Match format of 24 regulation rounds; first to 13 wins.

items.name: Pistol round
items.detail: First round of each half, with $800 each.

items.name: Sub-tick
items.detail: CS2 system that timestamps inputs between server ticks.

items.name: Tagging
items.detail: Being slowed when hit.

items.name: Recoil
items.detail: How the weapon kicks while firing; follows a fixed pattern per gun.

items.name: Inaccuracy (spread)
items.detail: Random deviation of bullets, larger when moving, jumping or spraying.

items.name: Prefire map
items.detail: A practice map with bots placed on common angles (for example the Yprac Hub prefire mode).

items.name: aim_botz
items.detail: A popular workshop aim training map with configurable bots.

items.name: Freeze time
items.detail: Start of the round when players cannot move; 15 s in Competitive.

items.name: Buy time
items.detail: Time to buy at the start of the round; 20 s in Competitive.

items.name: Mid
items.detail: The middle area of a map connecting the sites.

items.name: Spawn
items.detail: Where a team starts the round.

items.name: Contact play
items.detail: Moving quietly until first contact, then hitting fast.

items.name: Bait
items.detail: Letting a teammate take the first fight so you can trade.

items.name: Zeus
items.detail: Zeus x27 taser; one-shot at very close range.

limitations: Frames are sampled every 2–3 seconds, so quick deaths and kills can be missed on screen; with Game State Integration on, your kills, deaths, rounds and money come from the game instead.

Killer Replay is off in Competitive and Premier, so fight details are read from the death panel, the freeze-cam, the kill feed and the radar; findings are probable, not certain, and untagged deaths are counted, never guessed.
Game State Integration sends only your own state while you play: no positions, no other players and no enemy information, which keeps the coach fair.
Map callouts and radar transforms come from the game files of 22 Oct 2026; Ancient and Anubis callouts are less certain. Check them after map updates.
Live tips only in Practice, Workshop maps and your own server with bots; everything online is reviewed after the match.
